I have everything needed. Here is my thorough report.

## Owner identity: how `customerCode` and derived values are built

### 1. Files referencing the identity terms

Core identity classes (the "derivers"), all in `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/`:
- `CheckDigit.java` — Luhn check digit
- `MembershipNumber.java` — membership number
- `MembershipLevel.java` — numeric level 1-3
- `MembershipTier.java` — SILVER/BRONZE
- `Locality.java` — postcode/city → region
- `HouseholdId.java` — SHA-256 household id
- `IdentityKey.java` — duplicate-detection key
- `ContactPreference.java` — EMAIL/PHONE
- `OwnerMapper.java` — wires all of the above into the DTO

Owner request-pipeline functions in `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/`:
- `AssignCustomerCode.java` — builds `customerCode` (the actual generator)
- `CountNamesakes.java` — sets `namesakeCount`
- `HouseholdTier.java` — GOLD-tier decision (uses `HouseholdId`)
- `NormalizeOwnerAddress.java` — canonicalizes address (feeds household id)
- `RejectInvalidPostcode.java` — postcode/region validation (uses `Locality`)
- `RejectDuplicateHousehold.java` — household duplicate rejection
- `SaveOwner.java` — persists and writes the **AUDIT** log line
- `BuildOwner.java` — maps the DTO to entity, sets registration date

Model / config / spec:
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` — holds `customerCode`, `namesakeCount`, `registrationDate`, `postcode`, etc.
- `src/main/resources/openapi.yml` (lines ~2028, 2090-2156) — DTO field descriptions for every derived value
- `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml` — the pipeline wiring
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/escalation/InvalidPostcodeException.java`

Tests:
- `src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java` — the one live identity test
- `src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java` — test harness with `sha256hex`, `shaHex`, `luhn`, region/postcode tables
- `src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AuditLogCapture.java` — captures the `AUDIT` logger

### 2. The class that builds `customerCode` (current implementation)

`AssignCustomerCode.java` produces `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`: upper-cased first 3 letters of city, of last name, then a per-city 4-digit sequence = count of owners already in that city + 1:

```java
String city3 = prefix3(owner.getCity());
String last3 = prefix3(owner.getLastName());
int sequence = countInCity(owner.getCity(), ownerRepository) + 1;
owner.setCustomerCode(String.format("%s-%s-%04d", city3, last3, sequence));
```

Note a discrepancy worth flagging: the code emits `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`, but `openapi.yml` (line 2092) documents `customerCode` as `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` with a **global** sequence and example `FRA-0007`. The docs and code disagree on format and on per-city vs global sequence.

Everything derived from `customerCode`:
- **Membership number** — `MembershipNumber.of(customerCode, registrationDate)` returns `<customerCode>-M<YY>` (YY = last two digits of registration year), e.g. `SMI-0007-M26`. Pure function, no stored state.
- **Check digit** — `CheckDigit.of(customerCode)` is a standard Luhn check digit over the digits in `customerCode` (non-digits skipped), returning `(10 - sum%10) % 10`.

Other derived identity:
- **Locality / region** — see item 4 below.
- **Household id** — `HouseholdId.of(lastName, address)`: normalizes both (trim, collapse whitespace, lowercase), joins with `|`, SHA-256, and returns `H-` + first 6 bytes as hex (12 hex chars), e.g. `H-3f9a2b7c1e5d`.
- **Membership level / tier**, **contact preference**, **identity key** — all pure functions in the mapper package.

### 3. The audit record

There is no audit table; the "audit record" is a log line. `SaveOwner.service` saves the owner then writes to a dedicated SLF4J logger named `AUDIT`:

```java
private static final Logger audit = LoggerFactory.getLogger("AUDIT");
...
ownerRepository.save(owner);
audit.info("owner created id={} customerCode={} registrationDate={}",
        owner.getId(), owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate());
```

Tests assert on this via `AuditLogCapture` (attaches a Logback `ListAppender` to the `AUDIT` logger).

### 4. Postcode → region derivation

`Locality.java` is the single source:
- Postcode preferred: a 4-digit postcode maps by range — NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099.
- Fallback city table when postcode absent/out of range: Sydney→NSW, Melbourne→VIC, Brisbane→QLD, else `UNKNOWN`.
- `of(postcode, city)` tries postcode first, then `of(city)`.

The same ranges are duplicated in `RejectInvalidPostcode.java`, which rejects (400, `InvalidPostcodeException`) a 4-digit postcode outside the range for the city's region; absent postcode or unknown-region city accepts any 4-digit value. The test harness `AcceptanceBase` pins identical tables (`CITY_REGION`, `REGION_POSTCODES`, `REGION_TIMEZONE`).

The mapper exposes this as the DTO field `locality` (OpenAPI line 2131).

### 5. Full source of the core identity classes and test files

The complete contents of all of these were read in this session and are reproduced by path below (key snippets inline; the exact source of each is shown above in the tool results):

- `mapper/CheckDigit.java` — Luhn over customerCode digits (shown in full above).
- `mapper/MembershipNumber.java` — `String.format("%s-M%02d", customerCode, registrationDate.getYear() % 100)`.
- `mapper/Locality.java` — postcode-range + city-table region derivation (shown in full above).
- `mapper/HouseholdId.java` — SHA-256 `H-`+6-byte hex (shown in full above).
- `mapper/IdentityKey.java`, `mapper/MembershipLevel.java`, `mapper/MembershipTier.java`, `mapper/ContactPreference.java` — small pure functions (shown in full above).
- `mapper/OwnerMapper.java` — MapStruct `@Mapping` expressions calling each deriver:
  - `membershipNumber` = `MembershipNumber.of(owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate())`
  - `checkDigit` = `CheckDigit.of(owner.getCustomerCode())`
  - `locality` = `Locality.of(owner.getPostcode(), owner.getCity())`
  - `householdId` = `HouseholdId.of(owner.getLastName(), owner.getAddress())`
  - plus `identityKey`, `membershipLevel`, `contactPreference`, `displayName`, `initials`.
- `rest/function/owner/AssignCustomerCode.java` — the customerCode generator (shown in full above).
- `rest/function/owner/SaveOwner.java` — audit log line (shown in full above).
- `test/.../AcceptanceTest.java` — full file (17 lines) shown above. The only identity test currently present asserts customerCode matches `[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9A-F]{8}` (i.e. `<REGION>-<HASH8>`). The class Javadoc states a **redesign target**: "Redesign owner identity. The customerCode must become '<REGION>-<HASH8>'..." — this does NOT match the current `AssignCustomerCode` output (`<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`), so this test is a pending/failing spec driving a change.
- `test/.../AcceptanceBase.java` — full file (322 lines) shown above; provides `sha256hex`, `shaHex(s, n)` (first n upper-case hex of SHA-256), `luhn`, and the pinned region/postcode/timezone/holiday tables.
- `test/.../AuditLogCapture.java` — full file shown above.

### Key finding / likely intent
The acceptance spec wants `customerCode` reshaped to `<REGION>-<HASH8>` (region from `Locality` + first 8 upper-case hex chars of a SHA-256), replacing the current `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` per-city-sequence scheme in `AssignCustomerCode.java`. Because `MembershipNumber` and `CheckDigit` derive from `customerCode`, changing its format changes their outputs too. The OpenAPI `customerCode` description (line 2092) also still documents the old `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` form and would need updating. The SHA-256 helper already exists in `HouseholdId` and in the test harness (`shaHex`).

## Changes (2 files)

**`AssignCustomerCode.java`** — replaced the old `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` per-city-sequence scheme with the new region-and-hash identity:

- `HASH8` = first 8 upper-case hex chars of `SHA-256(normalizedTelephone + lastName)` — 4 digest bytes formatted with `%02X`.
